body:
Read the following passage and **correct any subject–verb agreement (concord) errors**. Do not copy the whole passage.

> There are literally a multitude of myths and dogmas which purposes to explain racial differences. They ranges from biblical explanations to zoological classifications. As one explanation loses its novelty or its power to convince, another emerge. The persistence of race theorists, as well as racists, are astonishing. Why do racists go to such lengths to find proof for what they obviously take for granted? Racism begins with the attempt to attach values to real or imaginary differences, and attempt to plumb the depth of absurdity when it produces a statement like, 'the race which is hairy is inferior to and less human than that which is free from body hair'.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. _myths and dogmas which **purposes**_ → **purport/purpose** (plural antecedent: _which purport to explain_).
> 2. _They **ranges**_ → **range**.
> 3. _another **emerge**_ → **emerges** (_another_ [explanation] is singular).
> 4. _The persistence of race theorists, as well as racists, **are**_ → **is** (head noun _persistence_).
> 5. _Racism begins … and **attempt** to plumb_ → **attempts** (parallel with _begins_; subject _racism_).
>
> (_There are … a multitude of myths_ is acceptable since _myths and dogmas_ is the notional plural subject; _one explanation loses_ and _racists go_ are correct.)
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Concord rules: the verb agrees with the **head noun** of the subject, ignoring intervening phrases; **compound subjects** with _and_ are plural; parenthetical additions (_together with, as well as, in conjunction with_) do not change the number; **relative pronouns** agree with their antecedents; in _there is/are_ sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows; modal verbs and _to_-infinitives take the **base form**.

## Simplified explanation

Fix: **which purport**, **they range**, **another emerges**, **persistence is**, **racism … attempts**.
hint: Find the head noun of each subject.

Read the following passage and **correct any subject–verb agreement (concord) errors**. Do not copy the whole passage.

> The number of motor accidents on our roads, especially major trunk roads such as the Accra-Kumasi, Accra-Takoradi, and Accra-Aflao highways keep rising with each passing day. The situation during Christmas and other traditional festivals when many Ghanaians travel to their hometowns to celebrate occasions and cultural festivities gets worse. A combination of factors account for this unfortunate phenomenon which invariably result in loss of lives and material resources. Human error as well as mechanical defects like faulty brakes, faulty lights, and worn-out tyres have been identified as being the most prominent among the factors. Statistics from the National Road Safety Commission show that ninety percent of all road accidents are due to carelessness on the part of the driver; over-speeding, over-loading, and wrong over-taking, coupled with drunkenness, tiredness, and poor sightedness, all these are attributed to the driver.
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. _The number of motor accidents … **keep** rising_ → **keeps** (_the number of_ + singular verb).
> 2. _A combination of factors **account**_ → **accounts** (head noun _combination_).
> 3. _this unfortunate phenomenon which invariably **result**_ → **results** (antecedent _phenomenon_).
> 4. _Human error as well as mechanical defects … **have** been identified_ → **has** (_as well as_ is additive, not conjunctive; the head is _human error_).
>
> (_The situation … gets worse_, _Statistics … show_ and _ninety percent of all road accidents are_ are correct.)

## Advanced explanation

Concord rules: the verb agrees with the **head noun** of the subject, ignoring intervening phrases; **compound subjects** with _and_ are plural; parenthetical additions (_together with, as well as, in conjunction with_) do not change the number; **relative pronouns** agree with their antecedents; in _there is/are_ sentences the verb agrees with the noun that follows; modal verbs and _to_-infinitives take the **base form**.

## Simplified explanation

Fix: **the number … keeps**, **combination accounts**, **phenomenon … results**, **human error as well as … has**.
